title: Why data alone does not convince anyone

videos.script: An analyst spends three weeks on a question. The data is clean, the numbers are right, and the finding matters. {{analyst}} She presents it in the monthly meeting. Thirty-eight slides, most of them tables. The room nods. {{nods}} Nobody decides anything. A month later the same problem is on the agenda, and so is she. {{again}} Nothing in that analysis was wrong. What was missing is the part this course is about. What the numbers mean, for whom, and what somebody should do on Monday. {{gap}} This lesson looks at why a correct number so often changes nothing. It introduces Faro, the company whose analysis you will carry through all sixteen lessons. {{faro}} And it ends with your own workbench. A folder, a spreadsheet, a slide tool and the data, set up on your own computer. {{workbench}}
